neighborhoods.name: Upper East Side
neighborhoods.description: The Upper East Side is one of Manhattan's most prestigious residential neighborhoods, renowned for its tree-lined streets, pre-war architecture, and proximity to Central Park. This refined enclave offers a sophisticated lifestyle with world-class museums, boutique shopping, and acclaimed dining.
neighborhoods.vibe: Elegant and refined with a family-friendly atmosphere. Quiet tree-lined streets contrast with the bustling avenues. A mix of longtime residents and young professionals seeking classic Manhattan living.

attractions.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
attractions.description: One of the world's largest and finest art museums with over 5,000 years of art

attractions.name: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum
attractions.description: Frank Lloyd Wright's iconic spiral building housing modern art masterpieces

attractions.name: Central Park
attractions.description: 843 acres of green space with running paths, playgrounds, and the Reservoir
attractions.address: Fifth Avenue to Central Park West

attractions.name: Brearley School
attractions.description: Prestigious all-girls K-12 independent school founded in 1884

attractions.name: Chapin School
attractions.description: Elite all-girls school founded in 1901

neighborhoods.name: Upper West Side
neighborhoods.description: The Upper West Side embodies the intellectual and artistic spirit of Manhattan. Home to Lincoln Center, Columbia University, and the American Museum of Natural History, this neighborhood attracts creatives, academics, and families seeking a vibrant cultural community.
neighborhoods.vibe: Artsy, intellectual, and community-focused. A laid-back alternative to the Upper East Side with notable cultural institutions, parks, and a strong sense of community.

attractions.name: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts
attractions.description: World-renowned performing arts complex featuring opera, ballet, symphony, and theater

attractions.name: American Museum of Natural History
attractions.description: Iconic museum with dinosaur fossils, the Hayden Planetarium, and extensive natural collections

attractions.name: Riverside Park
attractions.description: Four-mile waterfront park with playgrounds, sports fields, and stunning Hudson River views

attractions.name: Trinity School
attractions.description: America's fifth-oldest school, consistently ranked among the best independent schools

attractions.name: Columbia University
attractions.description: Ivy League research university founded in 1754

neighborhoods.name: Tribeca
neighborhoods.description: Tribeca (Triangle Below Canal) has evolved from industrial warehouses to Manhattan's most expensive residential neighborhood. Its cobblestone streets, cast-iron buildings, and converted loft spaces attract celebrities, financiers, and families seeking space and privacy in downtown Manhattan.
neighborhoods.vibe: Ultra-exclusive yet surprisingly family-friendly. Celebrity sightings are common, but the neighborhood maintains a village-like feel with excellent parks, schools, and a strong community spirit.

attractions.name: Tribeca Film Festival
attractions.description: Annual film festival founded by Robert De Niro to revitalize Lower Manhattan

attractions.name: Hudson River Park
attractions.description: Waterfront park spanning 5 miles with piers, playgrounds, and sports facilities

attractions.name: Pier 25
attractions.description: Tribeca's largest pier featuring mini-golf, beach volleyball, and a playground
attractions.address: West Street at N. Moore Street

attractions.name: Tribeca Grill
attractions.description: Legendary restaurant co-owned by Robert De Niro

attractions.name: PS 234 Independence School
attractions.description: Top-rated public elementary school

neighborhoods.name: SoHo
neighborhoods.description: SoHo (South of Houston) is famous for its stunning cast-iron architecture, world-class galleries, and high-end shopping. Once an industrial district, then an artist enclave, today it's a sophisticated neighborhood where art, fashion, and luxury converge.
neighborhoods.vibe: Trendy and artistic with a high-fashion edge. Streets are filled with tourists and shoppers during the day, transforming into a sophisticated dining and nightlife scene after dark.

attractions.name: Drawing Center
attractions.description: The only not-for-profit museum focused solely on the exhibition of drawings

attractions.name: SoHo Cast-Iron Historic District
attractions.description: The largest collection of cast-iron architecture in the world

attractions.name: Apple Store SoHo
attractions.description: Flagship Apple store in a historic building

attractions.name: MoMA Design Store
attractions.description: Design and art products curated by the Museum of Modern Art

attractions.name: New York City Fire Museum
attractions.description: Housed in a 1904 firehouse with artifacts dating to the 18th century

neighborhoods.name: Chelsea
neighborhoods.description: Chelsea is Manhattan's art gallery capital, with over 200 galleries concentrated west of Tenth Avenue. The neighborhood is also home to the High Line, Chelsea Market, and a thriving LGBTQ+ community. It offers a perfect blend of creativity, cuisine, and urban living.
neighborhoods.vibe: Artsy, progressive, and vibrant. A hub for the creative class with a strong community feel. Weekends see art lovers gallery-hopping while foodies explore Chelsea Market.

attractions.name: The High Line
attractions.description: Elevated linear park built on historic freight rail lines with art installations

attractions.name: Chelsea Market
attractions.description: Indoor food hall and shopping mall in a former Nabisco factory

attractions.name: Gagosian Gallery
attractions.description: Premier contemporary art gallery with locations worldwide

attractions.name: Whitney Museum of American Art
attractions.description: Premier museum of 20th and 21st-century American art

attractions.name: Hudson River Park
attractions.description: Waterfront park with sports facilities and Chelsea Piers

neighborhoods.name: Midtown
neighborhoods.description: Midtown is the commercial heart of Manhattan, home to iconic landmarks like the Empire State Building, Rockefeller Center, and Times Square. While known for business, it also offers luxury residential options with unmatched convenience and world-class amenities.
neighborhoods.vibe: Fast-paced and cosmopolitan. The energy of Times Square contrasts with quieter residential pockets near the East River. Ideal for those who want to be in the center of it all.

attractions.name: Empire State Building
attractions.description: Iconic 102-story Art Deco skyscraper with observation decks

attractions.name: Rockefeller Center
attractions.description: Historic complex with Top of the Rock, ice skating, and NBC Studios

attractions.name: The Museum of Modern Art (MoMA)
attractions.description: World's most influential museum of modern art

attractions.name: Grand Central Terminal
attractions.description: Beaux-Arts masterpiece and major transit hub

attractions.name: Bryant Park
attractions.description: Beloved public park with seasonal activities and free events

neighborhoods.name: Financial District
neighborhoods.description: The Financial District has transformed from a purely commercial area into a vibrant residential neighborhood. Historic landmarks like the New York Stock Exchange stand alongside modern luxury towers, offering waterfront living with quick access to all of Manhattan.
neighborhoods.vibe: Professional and polished during the week, surprisingly quiet and family-friendly on weekends. New restaurants and amenities have made it increasingly attractive for residents.

attractions.name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum
attractions.description: Memorial and museum honoring the victims of the September 11 attacks

attractions.name: One World Observatory
attractions.description: Observation deck atop the Western Hemisphere's tallest building

attractions.name: Battery Park
attractions.description: 25-acre waterfront park with gardens and views of the Statue of Liberty

attractions.name: Federal Hall National Memorial
attractions.description: Site where George Washington was inaugurated as the first U.S. President

attractions.name: Stone Street
attractions.description: Historic cobblestone street with outdoor dining and bars

neighborhoods.name: Greenwich Village
neighborhoods.description: Greenwich Village is one of New York's most desirable and historic neighborhoods. Known for its bohemian past, winding streets, and charming townhouses, 'The Village' offers a perfect blend of history, culture, and vibrant nightlife.
neighborhoods.vibe: Eclectic and charming with a strong artistic heritage. Tree-lined streets, intimate cafes, and hidden jazz clubs create a village-within-the-city atmosphere that residents cherish.

attractions.name: Washington Square Park
attractions.description: Iconic park with the Washington Square Arch, a hub of activity and culture

attractions.name: Blue Note Jazz Club
attractions.description: World-famous jazz club that has hosted legends for over 40 years

attractions.name: Comedy Cellar
attractions.description: Legendary comedy club where top comedians perform nightly

attractions.name: New York University (NYU)
attractions.description: Major private research university centered around Washington Square

attractions.name: Stonewall Inn
attractions.description: National Historic Landmark and birthplace of the LGBTQ+ rights movement
